item.title: 15 Bulikula Rugby League World Cup players still fighting for finals glory
item.description: The Fiji National Rugby League confirmed this to fijivillage News, saying with the 2026 Rugby League World Cup now fast approaching, 15 members of the Bulikula squad remain in finals contention across the NRLW, Queensland’s BMD Premiership and the NSW Women’s Premiership. They say for Fiji, it is an encouraging sign of the depth and quality available to the national women’s programme.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji National Rugby League confirmed this to fijivillage News, saying with the 2026 Rugby League World Cup now fast approaching, 15 members of the Bulikula squad remain in finals contention across the NRLW, Queensland’s BMD Premiership and the NSW Women’s Premiership.

They say for Fiji, it is an encouraging sign of the depth and quality available to the national women’s programme.

The Bulikula will make history this year by appearing at their first Rugby League World Cup after qualifying through the 2025 World Series in Canada.

Fiji thrashed Nigeria 62–4 in the final to secure the final women’s World Cup berth.

FNRL says that as preparations for the World Cup intensify, a number of Fiji’s players are still chasing domestic titles with their respective clubs.

The Women's Rugby League World Cup starts on the 8th of October , and runs through November 24, 2026.

item.title: Buadromo named IOC Believe in Sport Ambassador for Dakar 2026

item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s Olympic swimmer Matelita Buadromo has been named one of six IOC Believe in Sport Ambassadors for the Youth Olympic Games Dakar 2026 and is the only ambassador from Oceania.

Believe in Sport is an International Olympic Committee campaign aimed at tackling competition manipulation, which can involve athletes deliberately underperforming or losing, or officials deliberately making incorrect calls.

Buadromo represented Fiji in swimming at the London 2012 and Rio 2016 Olympic Games.

She has been involved in efforts to tackle competition manipulation since 2022, and her ambassador role will continue through the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, Pacific Games Tahiti 2027 and LA28.

In Dakar, the ambassadors will meet with young athletes, coaches and families to discuss how athletes can be approached in relation to competition manipulation and where such approaches can be reported.

Around 2,700 young athletes will compete in Dakar from 31st October to 13th November, in what will be the first Olympic sports event held on African soil.

Rewa to use BOG final defeat as motivation for IDC defence-Waranaivalu
item.description: Rewa coach Ratu Tevita Waranaivalu says his players can use their Extra Battle of the Giants final defeat as motivation as they prepare to defend their Inter District Championship (IDC) title. Waranaivalu says the team went through injuries, suspensions, sickness and other challenges during the two week tournament but managed to reach the final.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa coach Ratu Tevita Waranaivalu says his players can use their Extra Battle of the Giants final defeat as motivation as they prepare to defend their Inter District Championship (IDC) title.

Waranaivalu says the team went through injuries, suspensions, sickness and other challenges during the two week tournament but managed to reach the final.

He says the players gave everything for the team and he is proud of their effort despite the result.

Waranaivalu says the defeat should not be about blaming individuals, but about learning from mistakes and returning stronger.

He also expressed his graitutde to the officials, families, friends and supporters who stood behind the side.

Waranaivalu says Rewa now has three weeks to work harder, improve and prepare for the IDC, where they will defend their title.

The Inter-District Championship will be held from 6th to 11th October.

item.title: Flying Fijians turn attention to Japan after Canada victory
item.description: Acting Coach Senirusi Seruvakula says they will be looking to build on the positives from their win over Canada. Japan are expected to provide a different challenge, with their pace, discipline and attacking style likely to test Fiji across the field.
item.content:encoded:
Acting Coach Senirusi Seruvakula says they will be looking to build on the positives from their win over Canada.

Japan are expected to provide a different challenge, with their pace, discipline and attacking style likely to test Fiji across the field.

He says Fiji will be aiming to maintain their winning momentum and put themselves in a strong position as they battle for honours in the Pacific Nations Cup.

Fiji will face Japan in the finals this Saturday at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo at 7.05pm.

Bula FC congratulates Ba on BOG triumph
item.description: Extra Bula FC has congratulated Dayals Steel Ba FC after the Men in Black were crowned Extra Battle of the Giants champions, defeating Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC 2–1 and claiming the title on home ground. Bula FC says Ba's victory was a special moment as the team lifted the trophy in front of its home supporters.
item.content:encoded:
Extra Bula FC has congratulated Dayals Steel Ba FC after the Men in Black were crowned Extra Battle of the Giants champions, defeating Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC 2–1 and claiming the title on home ground.

Bula FC says Ba's victory was a special moment as the team lifted the trophy in front of its home supporters.

The club has also congratulated Rewa for finishing runners-up after a competitive tournament and battling until the final whistle.

Bula FC also acknowledges Seaqaqa FC following its Senior Extra League Final Play-Off victory, which secured the side’s promotion to the Premier League for the 2027 season.

The club has congratulated all the teams, players, coaches, officials and supporters involved in the tournament.

item.title: Pro Ref admits error in Haaland’s controversial derby winner
item.description: The English Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error of judgement in awarding Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City against Manchester United. Haaland’s 60th-minute goal was initially ruled out for offside before VAR intervened and determined he had been played onside by Patrick Dorgu.
item.content:encoded:
The English Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error of judgement in awarding Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City against Manchester United.

Haaland’s 60th-minute goal was initially ruled out for offside before VAR intervened and determined he had been played onside by Patrick Dorgu.

However, questions were raised over whether the offside Enzo Fernandez had interfered with play while diving towards the ball.

Pro Ref says although Fernandez did not touch the ball, the VAR failed to recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

United defender Lisandro Martinez described the decision as an injustice, while manager Michael Carrick says he was confused by the call.

City secured the derby victory despite playing with 10 men after Phil Foden was shown a straight red card in the 23rd minute for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.
